subject: Order Form redlines & IP carveouts — Odyssey Health
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen@odysseyhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form redlines — output & training questions

Marissa,

Thanks for the draft order form. A couple of items bubbled up from our product and legal teams that we need clarity on before we can move to procurement:

- Output ownership: the redline we received currently says Redwood assigns 'title' to outputs to the customer, but our legal team is asking about downstream productization rights — do we retain any license to reuse the outputs for model improvements?
- Training/data use: the default MSA language references a broad 'feedback' license. We need either a clear opt-in for training or an explicit carveout so that customer content is not used to train models without consent.
- Feedback license scope: if Redwood retains a telemetry/feedback license, can we get confirmation it is limited to aggregated, de-identified metrics and not raw customer content?

I've attached our redlines (Odyssey_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) and a mark-up of the MSA (MSA_redline_comments.docx). Can you propose amendment language that would be acceptable to both sides? We are trying to avoid holdups with procurement — target date for signature is end of month.

Happy to jump on a short call if it's easier.

— Ellen
Ellen Park
VP, Product — Odyssey Health
ellen@odysseyhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@odysseyhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-03-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form redlines — output & training questions

Ellen —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, received. Appreciate you flagging procurement timing; we'll prioritize. High-level responses and proposed path below:

1) Output ownership: we can confirm the Order Form will make explicit that Odyssey owns customer-specific outputs produced by the service (text, summaries, embeddings, etc.).

2) Training/data use: we can offer a narrow, opt-in training clause for model improvements. Suggested approach:
   - By default, Redwood will NOT use customer-provided content to further train or fine-tune public models.
   - Customer may opt in via a specific order form checkbox or an explicit exhibit, with granular scope (datasets, time window, revocation mechanics).

3) Feedback license: propose a limited telemetry/feedback license that permits Redwood to use aggregated, de-identified usage metrics and model performance signals solely to operate and improve the Redwood service. No raw customer content leaves the customer's control without explicit opt-in.

I'm attaching a short suggested redline snippet in the MSA comments (see attached). Two ask items for you: 1) confirm whether Odyssey requires any limited commercial rights to derivative models (e.g., if Redwood builds a vertical model using anonymized patterns, do you need a license), and 2) confirm the internal owner for the opt-in (legal, product, or procurement).

Looping in Laura (legal) and Karthik (sales/contract lead) to weigh in on specific clause language and timing. I can sync with your legal team Friday afternoon if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Marissa / Karthik —

I reviewed Odyssey's redlines. Below are suggested edits we should propose back to them (short, trackable changes):

1) Output ownership clause: Replace 'title' language with: "Customer shall own all Output generated by the Services that is specific to Customer's input data. Redwood grants Customer all rights necessary to use such Output for Customer's internal business purposes and to create derivative products." This keeps customer ownership but clarifies derivatives.

2) Training & feedback: Add an exhibit (Exhibit X) for Training Opt-In that requires: description of data, duration, revocation notice (30 days), and a separate fee if opt-in includes non-anonymized content. If Odyssey declines, default remains 'no training use'.

3) Feedback license: Add explicit limits: "Redwood's Feedback License is limited to aggregated, de-identified metrics and sample prompts/queries cannot be shared in identifiable form."

Operational notes: flag to Product that an opt-in could have billing/discount implications (Karthik). Also request a short questionnaire from Odyssey listing use cases where they require additional rights (e.g., building customer-specific hosted models).

I can draft track-changes in the MSA and the order form; Marissa, if you can confirm the commercial tradeoffs, I'll update the doc and send to Ellen and Odyssey Legal with a suggested compromise.

— Laura
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference

Ellen / Odyssey Legal —

Thanks again for the clear redlines. Per our internal review we've prepared a narrow counter-proposal and next steps:

1) Proposed changes (attached: MSA_redline_comments.docx):
   - Output: explicit customer ownership of Outputs; Redwood grants necessary rights to use the Output to deliver the Service.
   - Training: default = no training. Optional Exhibit X (Training Opt-In) that must be checked in the Order Form to allow any customer data to be used for model training; Exhibit X will specify scope, time window, and revocation mechanics.
   - Feedback license: limited to aggregated, de-identified signals used to operate and improve Redwood services; no sharing of raw, identifiable customer content.

2) Commercial/ops impact: if Odyssey opts into non-anonymized training or requires a transferable license to derivative Redwood models, there will be a pricing delta. Karthik's team will provide a pricing addendum once you confirm the exact opt-in scope.

3) Timeline & next steps:
   - We can send a tracked-change MSA + Order Form by EOD tomorrow.
   - If you want the opt-in exhibit, please send a short use-case note (1–2 bullets) so Commercial Ops can price it.
   - Proposal: quick sync Friday 3/18 at 11:00 AM PT to finalize language. Happy to book if that works for your team.

Please confirm whether Odyssey Legal prefers the tracked-changes or a clean side-by-side marked exhibit; we can do either.

Best regards,
